content: 1. Diazepam Interactions: Tetracycline increases the levels or effects of intranasal diazepam by inhibiting the CYP3A4 enzyme involved in its metabolism. This can lead to heightened adverse reactions. Close monitoring is advised. Metronidazole similarly increases the levels or effects of intranasal diazepam by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may slow the elimination of diazepam, increasing the risk of adverse effects. Monitoring is essential. 2. Dichlorphenamide and Bismuth Subsalicylate: Dichlorphenamide increases bismuth subsalicylate levels through an unknown mechanism. This combination is contraindicated. Co-administration of dichlorphenamide with high-dose aspirin may elevate salicylate levels, potentially causing anorexia, tachypnea, lethargy, or coma. Avoid this combination. 3. Metronidazole and Diclofenac: Metronidazole increases diclofenac levels by affecting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance is unclear, but monitoring is advised. 4. Tetracycline and Dicloxacillin: Tetracycline reduces the effects of dicloxacillin due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 5. Didanosine and Tetracycline: Didanosine decreases tetracycline levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both drugs. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Avoid simultaneous administration of oral tetracycline with didanosine chewable tablets or oral solution. 6. Metronidazole and Digoxin: Metronidazole increases digoxin levels by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 7. Tetracycline and Digoxin: Tetracycline also increases digoxin levels by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Caution and monitoring are advised. 8. Metronidazole and Dihydroergotamine: Metronidazole increases dihydroergotamine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination should be avoided or replaced with an alternative drug. 9. Metronidazole and Disulfiram: Disulfiram increases metronidazole toxicity by reducing its metabolism, leading to enhanced central nervous system and cardiac toxicity. This combination is contraindicated. 10. Metronidazole and Docetaxel: Metronidazole increases docetaxel levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unclear, but monitoring is advised. 11. Tetracycline and Doxycycline: Bismuth subsalicylate decreases doxycycline levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 12. Metronidazole and Dronabinol: Metronidazole increases dronabinol toxicity by inhibiting aldehyde dehydrogenase. This combination is contraindicated. Discontinue metronidazole at least 14 days before starting dronabinol solution and avoid administering metronidazole within 7 days of completing dronabinol treatment. 13. Metronidazole and Dronedarone: Metronidazole increases dronedarone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 14. Tetracycline and Drospirenone: Drospirenone increases tetracycline levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unclear, but monitoring is advised. 15. Metronidazole and Dutasteride: Metronidazole increases dutasteride levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unclear, but monitoring is recommended. 16. Efavirenz and Tetracycline: Efavirenz decreases tetracycline levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is advised. 17. Metronidazole and Efavirenz: Metronidazole increases efavirenz levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unclear, but monitoring is recommended. 18. Tetracycline and Elacestrant: Tetracycline increases elacestrant levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 19. Metronidazole and Elacestrant: Metronidazole increases elacestrant levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 20. Elagolix and Tetracycline: Elagolix decreases tetracycline levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 21. Metronidazole and Eletiptan: Metronidazole increases eletiptan levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 22. Tetracycline and Eliglustat: Tetracycline increases eliglustat levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 23. Metronidazole and Eliglustat: Metronidazole increases eliglustat levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 24. Bismuth Subsalicylate and Eluxadoline: These drugs increase each other's effects through pharmacodynamic synergy, raising the risk of constipation-related adverse reactions. Avoid co-administration with other constipation-inducing drugs. 25. Tetracycline and Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF: This combination increases tetracycline levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 26. Metronidazole and Fentanyl: Metronidazole increases fentanyl levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. If co-administration is necessary, monitor for respiratory depression and sedation, and adjust fentanyl dosage as needed. 27. Tetracycline and Fentanyl: Tetracycline increases fentanyl levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. If co-administration is necessary, monitor for respiratory depression and sedation, and adjust fentanyl dosage as needed. 28. Iron Supplements and Tetracycline: Iron supplements (e.g., ferrous fumarate, ferrous sulfate) decrease tetracycline levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 29. Metronidazole and Fluorouracil: Metronidazole increases fluorouracil toxicity by reducing its elimination. Caution and monitoring are advised. 30. Metronidazole and Ibuprofen: Metronidazole increases ibuprofen levels by inhibiting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance is unclear, but monitoring is recommended. 31. Tetracycline and Irinotecan: Tetracycline increases irinotecan levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 32. Metronidazole and Isavuconazonium Sulfate: Metronidazole increases isavuconazonium sulfate levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 33. Metronidazole and Isoniazid: Metronidazole increases isoniazid levels by inhibiting CYP2E1 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended.
